audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart says Graves owns Levels 1-2 ("Four shells of buckshot win any level-1 face-off"), but the packet chart and the prose whys both say Level 1 is Mel's and Levels 3, 4-5 and first item are Graves's outright, not "Skill".
audit.why: Graves's passive fires 4 bullets that cannot pass through units, so his damage only exists point-blank; Mel's Radiant Volley (Q) is a 950-range zone on a 10s cooldown at rank 1 and she has no reason to be inside 425. Level 1 with no Quickdraw is free poke for her. From 3, Quickdraw (E, 16s), Smoke Screen (W, 26s) and End of the Line (Q, 13s) let him close and cut her sight, which is his window.
audit.corrected: Chart: Mel / Skill / Graves / Graves / Skill / Graves / Mel — matching the packet chart and the existing whys.

audit.why: Spikes are placed at Lvl 1 (hers), Lvl 3 (his kit online), Lvl 6 (Golden Eclipse / Collateral Damage) and 2+ items (hers). That matches the kit cooldown structure and the win rate of 51.43% over 35 games.
audit.corrected: Kept the four spike timings; only the Level 6 and 2+ item text needed the ability-name fix.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer repeatedly states that Mel's R reflects damage and projectiles (whys[4], spikes[2], spikes[3], mid, wants.foe[1]). It does not. Golden Eclipse (R) strikes all enemies marked with Overwhelm regardless of distance and deals bonus damage per stack. The reflect is Rebuttal (W): a 250-range barrier that reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker, blocks damage and grants move speed, on 38/35/33/29/26s.
audit.why: Riot's own ability text in the kit file. Attributing the reflect to the ult tells a Graves player to hold his poke for a 120s cooldown when the real gate is a 38s W — and it hides the actual ult threat, which is a global execute-flavoured payout on Overwhelm stacks that kills him after he disengages at low HP.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal (W) is the reflect and the clock — 38s at rank 1. Golden Eclipse (R) is global and cashes Overwhelm stacks wherever you run, so never walk away from a trade on a sliver. Also: Graves's bullets cannot pass through units, so Mel's own minion wave shields her from the point-blank burst; End of the Line detonates on terrain, which is the only way to bend damage around it. Solar Snare (E, 1000 range, 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s) roots at its centre and slows around it — it is what denies Quickdraw's 425 dash.

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown advice names Rebuttal but gives no number, so "never poke while it glows" has no end.
audit.why: Rebuttal is 38s at rank 1 and only 26s at rank 5, while Graves's Quickdraw is 16s and refreshes off autos — the gap is enormous early and closes late. That number is what makes the advice actionable.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal is 38s at rank 1; once it is spent you own a long window.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer refers to Mel as "he"/"his" throughout (tldr, ahead, report entries).
audit.why: Mel is female; the pronouns read as a copy-paste from another matchup and undercut trust in the page.
audit.corrected: Fixed in the strings proposed below.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states that Graves's shotgun bullets cannot pass through units, which is the single mechanic that decides whether Mel can be punished at all.
audit.why: Riot's passive text: "Attacks fire 4 bullets, which cannot pass through units." Mel standing behind her own minions takes a fraction of the point-blank spread, so the closing play must come around or through the wave, not into it.
audit.corrected: Recorded in notes; the spike and phase rewrites push the player to close where no minion sits between them.

notes: Biggest fix: five places told the player Mel's ULT reflects damage and projectiles. It does not — Golden Eclipse (R, 120/100/80s, effectively global) strikes everyone marked with Overwhelm for bonus damage per stack. The reflect is Rebuttal (W, 250 range, 38/35/33/29/26s). The practical consequence is inverted advice: players were holding poke against a 120s cooldown instead of a 38s one, and were disengaging at low HP straight into the real ult threat. Packet defect ("never names any of Mel's abilities") is now addressed — Radiant Volley, Rebuttal, Solar Snare and Golden Eclipse all appear. Level chart was Skill x6 while the packet chart and the whys both said Mel/Skill/Graves/Graves/Skill/Graves/Mel; proposed as matched full+content pairs. Not proposed but worth a champion-level look: phases[4].why previously credited Collateral Damage with a "disengage knockback" — the knockback in Graves's kit is passive-only and applies to non-champions, so that phrasing may be wrong on other Graves matchups too. Also unmentioned anywhere on the page and left for a later pass: Solar Snare (E) roots at its centre, which is the tool that answers Quickdraw's 425 dash.
